A shape is a filtered view of one table that a client subscribes to. This route is a proxy in front of the sync service: which rows exist in the shape — the tenant, the lifecycle predicate, and the application's own scoping — is decided by the server and cannot be influenced from here. Where the client is in the stream is forwarded untouched.

With `live=true` the request is a long poll: it does not answer until something changes, so a client timeout set for an ordinary request will cut it short.

The response body is the sync protocol's own and is not described here. The `electric-*` response headers carry the cursor: send `handle` and `offset` back on the next request, or the subscription starts over.

Requires a session scoped to a tenant, and the shape is filtered to it.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where in the stream to resume, from the previous response's electric-offset.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The shape handle from a previous response. Omit it to start a new subscription.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: Long-poll until something changes, rather than answering with what is there now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The sync service's own cache-busting cursor, echoed back from the last response.

parameters.name: replica
parameters.description: Whether updates carry the whole row or only the columns that changed.

200.description: A chunk of the shape, in the sync protocol's own format.

electric-handle.description: The shape handle. Send it back to continue this subscription.

electric-offset.description: Where this chunk ended. Send it back to resume from here.

electric-cursor.description: The cursor to echo on the next request.

electric-up-to-date.description: Present when the client has caught up with the shape.

X-Rig-Sync-Fallback.description: Present when this response is a snapshot served because the sync service could not be reached, rather than a chunk of a live subscription. The rows are correct as of the moment they were read and are not updated until the subscription resumes.

502.description: The sync service could not be reached, and this shape had nothing to answer with instead: no database was configured, this shape asked not to be answered from one, or the read failed or was larger than a snapshot may be.

503.description: The sync service could not be reached, and this subscription already holds a snapshot. Keep it and retry after Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling again.

post.description:
The deletion stamp is cleared and the row appears in reads again. It works for 30 days after the deletion; past that the row is no longer eligible and this answers 409.

Restoring a row that was never deleted is not an error. It is already in the state the caller asked for, and answering otherwise would make a retry of a request whose response went missing look like a failure.

The request carries no fields. What to do when the world has moved on while the row was retired — a unique value taken by something created since — is the application's decision, and it is made in the restore hook: refuse, or change the row so that it fits.

Every rule then runs against whatever the hook settled on, not only the ones for fields it touched. The row was not live, so nothing about it has been checked against the world it is returning to.

Requires the `todo_attachment.write` permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the TodoAttachment.

post.summary: Attach a file to a TodoAttachment as its attachment.
post.description:
The form carries one part, named attachmentFile. Nothing else in it is accepted.

The type is sniffed from the bytes rather than taken from what the request claimed, and the sniffed type is what is stored and what a download announces. A file replacing an existing one does not delete it: a row that keeps its previous versions still points at the old file from every one of them.

Requires the `todo_attachment.attachment_file.write` permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the TodoAttachment.

requestBody.description: The file to attach, as a multipart form.

get.description:
Answers range and conditional requests, so a resumed download does not start over and a media element can seek.

Requires the `todo_attachment.attachment_file.read` permission.

parameters.description: Identifier of the TodoAttachment.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: Identifier of the file, from the row's attachment field.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The file's own name. It has to match the stored one, and it is what the browser offers to save the download as.

200.description: The file's bytes, announced as whatever they were sniffed to be.

206.description: The requested range of the file.

304.description: The caller already has this version of the file.

post.description:
Taking an item somebody else holds is a conflict rather than a
reassignment: two people picking up the same thing should not both be
told they have it. Taking one nobody holds is the ordinary case, and
taking one you already hold is not an error — a button pressed twice is
not a disagreement.

`steal` is the deliberate override, for the person who means it. It goes
through the same update as everything else, so the previous holder hears
about it the way they hear about any other change to their item.


Requires the `todo.claim` permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The item to take.

The deletion stamp is cleared and the row appears in reads again. It works for 30 days after the deletion; past that the row is no longer eligible and this answers 409.

bearerAuth.description:
A credential in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Two kinds are accepted and are told apart by a prefix on the token itself. A session access token travels on every request and is good for 10m, renewed against the session endpoints before it expires. An API key does not expire: an integration key's scopes are its permissions outright, and a personal key carries what its owner carries and no more.

The endpoints that issue and renew these are mounted under `/auth` and are not described in this document.
